history.dynasty: Ancient origins; Vijayanagara period (Krishnadevaraya's mukha mantapa, 16th century); Raja Vasireddi Venkatadri Nayudu (153 ft gopuram, 1807-1809)
history.summary: The hilltop shrine of Sri Panakala Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy on Mangalagiri ('The Auspicious Hill', ancient Thotadri/Totadri) is one of the 8 Mahakshetrams where Vishnu self-manifested. Mangalagiri holds three Narasimha shrines: the Panakala (hilltop), the Lakshmi Narasimha at the foot of the hill, and Gandala Narasimha at the very top. The presiding deity is a natural rock face worshipped as the Lord's open mouth; devotees pour Panakam (jaggery water) into it through a conch, and tradition holds that exactly half is accepted while half flows back as prasadam — with no ants or smell despite the sugar. Legend says the elephant-shaped hill is the transformed Hrusva Sringi (son of King Pariyatra), and Lakshmi did tapas here. A stone inscription of Sri Krishnadevaraya and the footprints of Mahaprabhu Chaitanya are on the steps. NOTE: the CSV town 'Guntur' is wrong — the temple is in the town of Mangalagiri, Guntur district. This row is the hilltop shrine of the same temple complex whose foot-of-hill shrine is documented in 13.json (Sri Mangalagiri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple) — near-duplicate of one complex, kept separate here as hilltop vs. foothill shrine; dedup decision needed.

name: Sri Panakala Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple
town_description: Mangalagiri ('The Auspicious Hill') is a temple town in Guntur district, about 12-13 km from Vijayawada, built around the elephant-shaped hill of the same name. It is famous for its three Narasimha shrines, the Lakshmi Pushkarini tank, and its handloom tradition — Mangalagiri sarees and cotton dress materials with zari borders are known across India.

travel.airport: Nearest airport is Vijayawada (Gannavaram), about 35 km away (per gotirupati.com; verify current connectivity).
travel.railway: Nearest major railhead is Guntur Junction (~21 km); Vijayawada Junction is the other major railhead (verify distances).
travel.road: Mangalagiri is ~13 km from Vijayawada and ~21 km from Guntur on the Vijayawada-Guntur road; the hilltop shrine is reached by a flight of steps (sources mention ~600 steps; verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for cool weather and a comfortable climb. The annual Brahmotsavam (February-March) is the most festive but most crowded period.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Panakala hill shrine: approximately 7:00 AM to 3:30/4:00 PM daily (panakam offering ends ~3:30 PM; the shrine closes early in the day — tradition says the devas worship here in the evening). Nijaroopa darshan at 6:00 AM on every Ekadasi (verify all timings on site).
